articles.summary: When CNN’s Kaitlan Collins approached President Trump with a question about the Iran war at the United Nations General Assembly yesterday, the president scolded her for being there at all. “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” Trump said, adding, “You should not be here covering me.” Presumably, he said this because CNN is among the three outlets , along with MS NOW and Politico , that Trump has barred from White House grounds because he didn’t like their coverage. But, to state the obvious, the United Nations is not the White House. If a journalist is denied a press pass from one entity, she’s not precluded from getting credentialed by another. As Collins said to Trump, “The United Nations allowed us in, sir.” The exchange highlights Trump’s warped understanding of journalism—in which stories are either good or bad, reporters are “ friendly ” or “ terrible ,” and a president decides who covers him and who doesn’t. “There’s something wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories,” he said when he banned CNN and the other two outlets. “Now, if they want to write them, that’s fine. But I don’t have to let them into my—into the people’s house.”

articles.summary: Republicans are playing defense deep in their own territory as voter anger over price hikes puts more House and Senate seats in play in the midterms. New rounds of big spending, visits from Trump administration officials and private conversations among top GOP officials overseeing the battle for control of Congress reveal a party rushing to shore up red seats and states President Donald Trump won handily in 2024.
